title: The Witch Who Knew Too Much

junior.scene: The edge of the valley, nighttime. Fog everywhere.

paragraphs.c: Venusaur couldn't sleep. He kept thinking about Charizard and those weird burn marks on his claws.
So tonight, he decided to follow Charizard. Like a detective! A really big, really slow, really loud detective.
The sun went down. The stars came out. And sure enough — Charizard woke up, stretched his wings, and flew north.
Venusaur tried to sneak through the forest after him. But sneaking is hard when you weigh as much as a car.
CRUNCH. SNAP. CRUNCH.
"You know, for a spy, you're really, REALLY bad at this."
Venusaur froze. That voice came from... everywhere? He looked left. He looked right. He looked up.
And there she was.
— purple mist swirls and sparkles fill the air —

Mismagius floated down from the treetops, covered in sparkles and glowing purple light. She was a Ghost-type who'd lived in the valley forever. Nobody knew where she came from. She just... showed up wherever something interesting was happening.
Some Pokémon called her the Witch. She preferred "Observer."

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "You're following the big dragon, aren't you?"

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "I'm INVESTIGATING. That's different."

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Sure, sure. Very professional. Very sneaky. Not at all like a Tauros crashing through a gift shop."
Venusaur's face got hot. His flower started blooming. That always happened when he was embarrassed.

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "Do you know what Charizard is doing every night?"
Mismagius stopped smiling. Her sparkles changed from pink to dark purple. She floated closer.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "I know EVERYTHING that happens in this valley at night. I know Charizard flies to the northern caves to keep the baby Pokémon warm. But that's not the scary part."

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "There's a SCARY PART?"

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Something new has come to the valley. Something made of metal. It has a cannon on its back. It doesn't eat. It doesn't sleep. It just flies around scanning everything. And it's heading straight for those caves."
— SCREEEEECH! A metallic sound echoes from the mountains —
They both looked up. A streak of purple and silver light shot across the sky like a rocket. It wasn't a bird. It wasn't a Pokémon they'd ever seen. It moved like a machine — fast, sharp, and scary.
Genesect. A robotic Pokémon with a giant cannon on its back, blasting through the sky straight toward the northern caves.
Straight toward Charizard. Straight toward the babies.

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "We have to warn Charizard! NOW!"

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "WE? Oh no no no. I'm a ghost. I float and I watch. I don't DO running."

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "Mismagius. Please."
She looked at him for a long moment. Then she sighed — a sigh that made all the flowers around them shiver.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Fine. But I'm floating the whole way. And if anything bad happens, I'm blaming you."
And so the grumpiest Pokémon in the valley and the spookiest Pokémon in the valley started running (and floating) north as fast as they could.
Behind them, the valley slept peacefully.
Ahead of them, Charizard had no idea what was coming.
And above them, Genesect's cannon glowed in the dark.
To be continued...

full.scene: The edge of Verdant Valley, twilight. Fog rolling in.

paragraphs.c: Venusaur couldn't sleep.

It had been three days since he'd noticed the scorch marks on Charizard's claws. Three days of watching that overgrown fire hazard nap in the meadow like he didn't have a care in the world. Three days of knowing something was off and not being able to prove it.
So tonight, Venusaur did something he'd never done in fourteen years of living in this valley. He followed someone.

The moment the sun dipped below the ridge and the last Pidgey stopped chirping, Charizard stirred. Stretched his wings. Yawned a column of fire that nearly scorched a passing Butterfree — "SORRY!" — and launched into the sky heading north.
Venusaur lumbered after him on the ground, sticking to the tree line, moving as quietly as a four-hundred-pound dinosaur plant possibly could. Which was not quietly at all.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "You know, for a spy, you're absolutely terrible at this."

The voice came from everywhere and nowhere. It floated down like silk made of smoke, curling around his ears with a warmth that felt... wrong. Too warm. The kind of warm that makes you forget what you were doing.
— the fog parts, and a swirl of purple mist takes shape —

Mismagius descended from the canopy, trailing sparkles and pink crystal light like she was her own special effect. Her eyes — those impossible red eyes — locked onto Venusaur with the expression of someone who had been watching this whole situation unfold for weeks and was deeply entertained by it.

Mismagius was the valley's oldest mystery. Nobody knew when she'd arrived. Nobody knew where she lived. She showed up at every major event — every argument, every breakup, every midnight scandal — and watched from the shadows with that little smile.
Some Pokémon called her the Oracle. Others called her the Witch. Snorlax once called her "deeply unsettling," which was the most words Snorlax had used in a single sentence all year.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "You're following the dragon."

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "I'm investigating. There's a difference."

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Mmm. Of course. Very official. Very dignified. Very much stumbling through bushes at midnight like a confused Tauros."
Venusaur felt his face go hot. Which, for a Grass-type, meant his flower actually started to bloom a little. Embarrassing.

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "Do you know what he's doing? The night flights? The scorch marks?"
Mismagius tilted her head. The sparkles around her shifted from pink to deep violet. When she spoke, her voice dropped to something almost serious.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "I know everything that happens in this valley after dark, Venusaur. Everything. I know that Charizard flies north every single night. I know what he does when he gets there. And I know that you're not going to like the answer — not because it's bad, but because it's going to make you feel guilty for every rotten thing you've said about him."
She drifted closer. The air around her got colder. The sparkles died.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "He's not just keeping them warm. He's guarding them. Something has been approaching the northern ridge for the past two weeks. Something none of us have ever seen before. Metal body. Red eyes. A cannon on its back. It doesn't eat. It doesn't sleep. It just... scans. Like it's searching for something."
Venusaur felt the vines on his back tighten involuntarily.
— a distant metallic screech echoes from the northern mountains —
Both of them turned toward the sound. Above the treeline, a streak of purple and silver light cut across the sky like a comet with a grudge. Fast. Precise. Nothing natural about it.

Genesect had arrived in Verdant Valley. Not walking. Not flying in the way birds fly — no grace, no wind. It moved like a machine that had calculated the most efficient trajectory between two points and simply executed. The cannon on its back glowed a sickly violet, scanning the terrain below.
It was heading straight for the northern caves. Straight for Charizard.

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "We have to warn him."

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "We? Oh no no no. You have to warn him. I'm an observer. I observe. I comment. I occasionally make things sparkle. I do not do... running."

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "Mismagius. Please."
She looked at him. Really looked at him — past the grumpy exterior and the judgmental squinting and the fourteen years of loudly complaining about Charizard at every community meeting.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "...You actually care about him, don't you?"
Venusaur said nothing. His flower bloomed a little more.

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Fine. But I'm floating. And if I die, I'm haunting you specifically."

paragraphs.speaker: Venusaur
paragraphs.c: "You're already a ghost."

paragraphs.speaker: Mismagius
paragraphs.c: "Then I'll haunt you harder."

They moved north. Venusaur running — actually running — for the first time in years. Mismagius gliding beside him, trailing purple light and looking like the most reluctant hero in the history of Verdant Valley.
Behind them, the valley slept peacefully. Ahead of them, a dragon who didn't know he needed saving was about to meet something that didn't know it needed stopping.
And above them all, Genesect's cannon hummed.
To be continued…
